identity.name: Acetylated oxidized starch
identity.chemical_class: Chemically modified starch (oxidized and acetylated starch derivative)

function.mechanism: Oxidation and acetylation of starch alter gel/texture properties and improve clarity and stability, supporting thickening and stabilization functions.
common_food_categories: processed foods using modified starches for texture
other foods where modified starch acts as emulsifier/stabilizer

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 re-evaluation of modified starches (including E1451) concluded no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels.

efsa.key_finding: E1451 was included in EFSA's modified-starch group re-evaluation; EFSA concluded no safety concern at reported uses/use levels and no numerical ADI required.

fda.notes: Regulated as food starch-modified under food additive provisions. Relevant conditions include oxidation and acetylation reagent limits; no explicit standalone CFR GRAS entry naming acetylated oxidized starch was identified in reviewed Part 182/184/186 exports.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA record shows ADI NOT SPECIFIED (2016 and 2001 entries); 2018 entry is specification-only.

concerns.summary: In a 90-day rat study summarized by JECFA, urinary bladder and kidney microscopic changes were reported at the highest dietary concentration; NOEL was 5900 mg/kg bw/day.
High-dose rat studies reported gastrointestinal-adaptive findings (soft feces, enlarged/dilated caeca) at elevated dietary levels.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA's 2017 re-evaluation did not identify a safety concern for modified starches (including E1451) at reported uses/use levels.
EFSA indicated no genotoxic concern for modified starches in its read-across framework.
JECFA retained ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for acetylated oxidized starch.

populations: High consumers of confectionery, including adolescents
adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI is established by EFSA/JECFA for this additive context; therefore numerical ADI exceedance cannot be directly calculated from these evaluations.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory assessments (EFSA/JECFA) are consistently permissive with no numerical ADI and no current IARC classification signal. Animal high-dose findings exist but were interpreted within a no-safety-concern conclusion at intended use levels.
key_factors: EFSA 2017 concluded no safety concern at reported use levels for modified starches including E1451
JECFA ADI is NOT SPECIFIED and latest update is specification-focused
FDA/eCFR regulates use via 21 CFR 172.892 with reagent/composition limits
No E1451-specific IARC monograph classification identified
Recent PubMed evidence is limited for direct modern E1451-specific toxicology
